 Lilia Sebouai is a reporter for The Telegraph’s Global Health Security and Foreign desks. She covers topics including infectious disease, emerging threats, humanitarian crises and conflict.
 Published 
 11 November 2026 2:08pm GMT
 Donald Trump’s officials have been accused of destroying documents to avoid scrutiny before the Democrats take power in Congress .
 Whistleblowers have said the interior department has been disposing of records on the US president’s legacy building projects in Washington DC before the new congress is sworn in in January.
 The interior department dismissed the claims as “100 per cent false”.
 House Democrats demanded that the department, which fast-tracked many of Mr Trump’s projects, preserve records on his construction around the capital, CNN reported.
 The projects, including a triumphal arch, a White House ballroom , a redesigned golf course, restoration of the Lincoln Memorial Pool and repaving of the Rose Garden, are estimated to cost more than $900m (£676m).
 On Tuesday, Jared Huffman, the top Democrat on the House natural resources committee, sent letters to private companies and federal agencies, asking them to preserve all records that the committee may need for oversight.
 All recipients have to reply to confirm their compliance.
 Mr Huffman said multiple whistleblowers had approached him in recent weeks about the documents.
 The interior department said it had followed all federal records management “as directed by the department’s ethics officials”.
 The committee, which oversees national parks and federal lands, is expected to lead the scrutiny of Mr Trump’s construction projects, along with the House oversight and judiciary committees.
 There are already talks of high-profile hearings to examine several projects including the golf course and 250ft-tall triumphal arch , which could cost as much as $100m, Axios reported.
 “Everything is coming; it’s all coming,” Mr Huffman told CNN. “It’s just going to be an entirely new day.”
 Administration moving at ‘lightning speed’
 The Trump administration is reportedly speeding up construction to lay as much groundwork as possible before the Democrats take control of Congress in January.
 Davis Ingle, the White House spokesman, said the administration was “moving at lightning speed” as they “don’t have time to waste in our mission to make America greater than ever before”.
 Charles Birnbaum, the president of the Cultural Landscape Foundation, said he expected many projects to move forward “simultaneously”.
 “It is going to be like a storm where it plays out until the new Congress is seated,” he said.
 Mr Trump’s personal construction projects, which include rebuilding the East Wing to include a new Marine One helipad, have already drawn widespread criticism.
 The cost of the East Wing alone would cost $600m, with half coming from taxpayers, the Washington Post reported.
 In December, Mr Trump doubled the size and cost of his proposed 90,000 sq ft ballroom to $400,000, citing “deep rooted studies” that showed the space needed to be expanded and upgraded in quality.
 The construction site of the White House ballroom, which is set to cost $400,000
 Credit : AP/Alex Brandon
 It will reportedly act as a “shield” for a massive multi-storey underground bunker and military complex.
 Last year, Jamie Raskin, the Democratic representative, criticised the plans, saying that the president was “tearing apart the people’s house to build a gaudy Marie Antoinette ballroom for the billionaires and CEOs to party”.
 Barack Obama, the former US president, also mocked Mr Trump’s interior aesthetic, saying: “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.”
